title: In-class DKA: Nora Whitcombe (new-onset type 1, 24 h, checkpoints every 4 hours)
diagnosis: Moderate-to-severe diabetic ketoacidosis (pH 7.14, bicarbonate 7, beta-hydroxybutyrate 6.8, anion gap 30) as the first presentation of type 1 diabetes
desc: Mon 02/08 0700 to Tue 02/09 0700 in seven 4-hour checkpoints (in class; bedside monitor MRN SIM-40602). A 22-year-old college student with 6 weeks of thirst, urinating and weight loss arrives from the ED in DKA with a new diagnosis of diabetes. Adult fixed-rate DKA protocol with a dextrose step, peripheral potassium riders, the anion gap and resolution criteria, diet advancement, the transition to basal-bolus insulin with overlap, the emotional side of a new chronic diagnosis, a first low glucose on subcutaneous insulin, and survival-skills teaching for discharge. Vital signs and bedside glucoses after 0700 come from the monitor and the instructor.
